notes.title: End of the Month Review - April 2022
notes.content:
Hello again, and welcome to our EotM Review for April 2022!

As many may have noticed, Board Game Engine runs on Unreal Engine 4. Earlier in April, Epic released the first stable release of Unreal Engine 5, something we had been watching with great anticipation here at Omnibox. When we were building Board Game Engine, we attempted to ensure compatibility with the upcoming UE5 release, though at the time we did not know when that would be. This month we finally had the opportunity to port all of our work to Unreal Engine 5! This build currently lives on the test branch and should sport performance improvements and minor graphical changes over the UE4 versions.

Also with UE5 came Epic's own Chaos Physics system, which allows much greater physics stability and precision. We are very pleased to be able to take advantage of this in Board Game Engine going forward, and in the newest test build and all future updates, we will be running on the Chaos system. With that in place, we will be much more comfortable allowing more dynamic physics situations in later updates.

Additionally, the multiplayer update is on the horizon, and we will be happily finishing up this major update in the new UE5 build. We are disappointed that it has taken this long but are pleased that it is finally coming to fruition. During the next month, much of our efforts will go towards that baseline documentation that everyone has been asking for. Of course, during this time you can always opt into the test builds to try out the updates early during this process!

As always, thank you everyone for your support! We look forward to delivering the next major update soon.

notes.title: End of the Month Review - March 2022
notes.content:
Welcome to our second End of the Month Review!

This March marked an important milestone in multiplayer development, with great success loading multiplayer games with minimal desync. With this successful test we move towards further bolstering multiplayer capabilities and preparing the user interface for additional multiplayer functionality. 

We have also determined that BGE documentation will be contained in a knowledge base online, this way it can be searched and archived easily and will be accessible ingame through Steam's web browser. We have also considered printing a little booklet for functions, but are forgoing this idea due to the speed at which such material would become outdated.

Once again we would like to thank you, our community, for your patience with our development. You are always more than welcome to try out multiplayer on the test branch while we continue to update it!

notes.title: End of the Month Review - Feb. 2022
notes.content:
This marks the first of a continuous series of End of the Month Reviews. We will use these monthly posts to let everyone know what we've been up to and where we are going. These will be especially helpful during quieter months, when there may be little to announce on a daily or weekly scale.

This February was a busy one here at Omnibox Games. We released five minor updates including various fixes to the editor, as well as updating grid support to work for both square and hex grids. 

As mentioned since launch, [b]multiplayer[/b] has been our highest priority and we have continued to progress towards that goal. What we can say so far, is multiplayer will be highly [b]Workshop based[/b]; usage of a save in multiplayer will require it being uploaded to the Workshop in some form. 

[u]Multiplayer is coming soon[/u], and with it, we plan to include a full [b]user manual[/b] with that update. For all future major updates, we will be including a fully up-to-date user manual detailing each and every feature of the engine. We have noted the needs surrounding tutorials and documentation, so we hope the upcoming manual will be helpful until we are able to create dedicated tutorials.

We are grateful for the amount of interest we have received already, and for those who have already picked up the engine package early. Thank you everyone for your support!

notes.title: We are Live!
notes.content:
We are pleased to announce the release of Alpha 1.0 of Board Game Engine!

As we are in Early Access and this is version 1.0, we anticipate bugs will quickly arise. We will do everything we can to squash bugs and smooth glitches. As promised, the editor is currently free while we work towards multiplayer, that is still our highest priority!

We have a long road ahead of us, but we hope you'll join us for the journey.
Thank you all for your continued support

notes.title: Launch Status Update
notes.content:
It’s an exciting time here at Omnibox, but it's easy to get swept up in the moment as a small team launching our first major digital project. We want to remain as transparent as possible with our potential users.

We have decided that it is in the best interest of our potential user and the overall health of the Board Game Engine at launch to delay multiplayer functionality until it is ready. To make up for this we have decided to launch the Board Game Engine Editor as free content until such a time that we can deliver a product worth your valuable time and money. Please note, that we are working diligently to meet our goals for the Board Game Engine and provide the best possible experience for our users; multiplayer is our highest priority. 

Again, we apologize for this delay but are still looking forward to launching the Board Game Engine on the 21st of January as intended. Keep a lookout for more updates as we continue to update the engine’s functionality and fix bugs in the coming weeks.

-The Omnibox Team

notes.title: Board Game Engine Release
notes.content:
[h1]Board Game Engine releases on January 21![/h1]

As per our planned monetization, all users will be able to download Workshop items and play with them for free. The editor itself is in a $9.99 DLC package. This was the easiest way to ensure a universal game Workshop while also keeping our free-to-play, pay-to-edit model.

[h2]Workshop Support[/h2]
As we enter our initial launch, we want to encourage everyone to share their components, in addition to their games, on the Workshop. As more items are added, the Workshop will be able to not only be a place to find games to play but also function as a massive free library of game components for developers to use when prototyping. We plan on releasing many content packs of our own on the Workshop over time, but nothing beats community support!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41707851/30377fb429e66999322552f0124546583421dd5a.jpg[/img]

[h2]Grid Support[/h2]
By popular demand, we are pushing to have support for grids in the initial release! You will be able to enable grids in your game settings, set the grid to square or hex, and scale it as needed.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41707851/630d14ac72a6322121800f3507e8e5534c73833a.jpg[/img]

[h2]Multiplayer[/h2]
Unfortunately, we have made the hard decision to delay multiplayer at launch. We feel multiplayer is incredibly important, so it will be our highest priority until implemented in the near future.

[h3]Thank you everyone for your support![/h3]
